newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sees 1997/98 trade gap at $2.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sees 1997/98 trade gap at $2.1 bln.

text.p: Pakistan is aiming to cut its trade gap to $2.1 billion in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) from more than $3 billion this year, a government document said.
The Annual Plan 1997/98, a copy of which was obtained by Retuers on Friday, said the reduction would be achieved by boosting exports by 15 percent and restraining growth in imports to five percent.
Pakistan recorded a provisional trade deficit of $3.149 billion in the first 11 months of 1996/97, official figures show.

The Annual Plan said next year's export growth target might seem high, but was justifiable because of an expected six percent increase in agriculture and manufacturing output, compared to the 1.2 percent growth estimated for this year.
It said imports, which totalled $10.67 billion in July-May 1996/97, would expand five percent to $12.4 billion in the whole of 1997/98.
The Plan said this estimate assumed some stability in prices of key imports such as crude oil, oil products and edible oils, as well as lower sugar imports due to higher domestic output.
